lawyer:
Mr. Farid Ahmed, Advocate, with Mr. Md. Emdadul Haque, Advocate ------ For the Petitioner. 
Mr. Abu Sayeed Ahmed, Advocate ------ For the Opposite Parties.
parties:
Maleka Banu and others ------ Petitioners.
Vs.
Lt. Col.(Retd.) Raziur Rahman and others ------ Opposite Parties.
full_judgment:
The petitioners as plaintiffs instituted a Suit being T.S. No. 172 of 1981 on 20.5.84 in the Court of the First Subordinate, Judge, Dhaka against the defendant opposite parties for declaration of their 16 annas title to the suit-lands described in the hedale of the plaint. Then, with the creation of Gazipur as a District, the suit was transferred to the Court of the subordinate Judge, Gazipur and renumbered as Title Suit No. 357 of 1985. The plaintiffs' case as appears from the plaint is, inter alia that the land in C.S. Plot No. 2071 measuring 12.81 acres originally belonged to the Zaminders of the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate. While in possession, the said Court of Wards Estate settled 2.39 acress of land from the said plot to one Mr. Taru Mohan by an amalnama dated 4.10.40. Thereafter, Taru Mohan sold the said land on 16.3.46 to the predecessors of the petitioners Keramat Ali and Samad Ali and made over possession of the same. After the death of Keramat Ali and Samed Ali, plaintiff petitioners Nos. 1-5 inherited the said properties. Further case of the plaintiffs is that one Haris Mia. Sultan and Raja Mia took pattan of .53 acres of land of the said plot from the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate. Haris Miah got the above land; on amicable settlement along with other ejmali lands and while in possession; he sold out the same to the plaintiffs Nos. 2-4. By a said deed date 5.2.66 and made over possession of the land to them. Further case of the plaintiff is that one Bhagaban Chandra Barman took pattan of 5.25 acres of land from the said Estate in 1351 B.S. and while in possession he sold out '70 acre of land to the plaintiff petitioner No. 1 on 28.5.45; He also sold out 1.58 acres of land to the aforesaid Sultan Raja Miah and Haris Miah on 11.3.46 by a registered deed and Miaju Mia sold out .70 acre of land to the plaintiff petitioners. Nos.2-5 by two registered deeds, dated 3.3.67 and 24.2.69 respectively. This way the plaintiff-petitioners Nos. 1-5 got 4.32 acres of land and plaintiff petitioner No. 6 got 88 acre of land. Thus, collectively all the plaintiff-petitioners acquired 5.20 acres of total in case plot No. 2071 and they are in exclusive possession of the same which has been recorded in their names during the S.A./ R.S. operations and they are also residing in some pinion of the said plot No. 2071 by constructing dwelling house and also by growing fruit bearing, trees in other portions. Further case of the plaintiffs is that the defendant No. 6, who is opposite party No. 1 in this case in collusion with other Opposite Parties No. 4 allegedly took settlement of four acres of land from the suit Plot No. 2071 and is now trying to take possession of the same by dispossessing the plaintiff-petitioners. Hence, the plaintiffs filed the aforesaid suit for declaration of their title to the suit lands and subsequently filed an application for temporary injunction to restrain the defendant Opposite Party Nos. 1 from interfering with their possession in the suit lands. Opposite party No. 1, i.e. defendant No: 6, entered appearance in the said suit and filed written objection against the application for temporary injunction denying all the material allegations in the application and contending, inter alia, that the suit lands originally belonged to the Bhawal Court of Words Estate which settled from the disputed C.S. Plot No. 2071 an area of 8.23 acres of lands to different persons and after the promulgation of State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, the remaining 4.58 acres of the lands were made khas according to the law and the same vested with the Government when defendant No. 6, the present opposite party No. 1, took permanent settlement of 4 acres of land out of 4.58 acres in plot No. 2071 through due process of law and also obtained actual physical possession of the same by demarcation of the lands with boundaries and pilfers and has been continuing in his possession over the same on payment of rents. Further case of the contesting defendant is that the plaintiff-petitioners have no right title or possession in the suit land and as such they have no prima facie case for injunction and the balance of convenience and inconvenience is not in their favour rather the same is in favour of the contesting defendant No. 6 and further, the lands upon which the injunction has been sought, for by the plaintiffs have not been clearly and correctly described and as such those are vague and indefinite. Hence, the application for injunction is not maintainable and the same is liable to be rejected. Both the sides filed some documents in support of their respective cases. The learned Subordinate Judge, after hearing both the parties in the matter of the application for injunction and on consideration of their submissions and the materials on record, he found that the contesting defendant No. 6 i.e. opposite party No. 1, after obtaining the permanent settlement of the land, has been put into possession by the Government in the said 4 acres of land in C.S. Plot No. 2071 and has also found from the Advocate Commissioner's report that the contesting defendant No. 6 has been possessing the said lands in C.S. Plot No. 2071 by demarcation and boundary pillars. The learned Subordinate Judge also found on scrutiny that the suit land, as claimed by the plaintiffs, has not been properly specified and described and that he application for temporary injunction is not maintainable as such. On the above findings, the learned Subordinate Judge was pleased to reject the application for temporary injunction on contest by his Judgment and order dated 18.6.88. On appeal, being Title Appeal No. 21 of 1988, by the plaintiff-petitioners before the learned Additional District Judge; Gazipur, who, after hearing the parties and on consideration of the materials on records, was pleased to find that the plaintiffs petitioners out of their alleged acquired 5.20 acres of land froth the disputed plot being C.S. Plot No. 2071 which originally belonged to the Bhawal Court of Wards Estate according to the plaintiffs, the Government acquired some lands for the C & B Department and Cotton Development Board for which, they got compensation but the said Board or the C & B authorities have not been made parties in this suit and that the plaintiffs appear to have been able to show only a duplicate carbon copy of their alleged pattan and a few dakhilas showing payment of rent only for some portion of the suit lands. The learned Additional District Judge concurrently found with. the Court of the first instance that out of the disputed plot, namely C.S. Plot No. 2071, 8.23 acres were settled with some persons and the rest 4.58 acres of lands of the Bhawal Court of Words Estate was made khas after the enforcement of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, and the same vested with the Government as khas lands out of which the contesting defendant opposite party No. 1 took permanent settlement of 4 acres of land and went into actual possession of the same by demarcation of boundaries and putting pillars and thus became a co-sharer in the suit plot. Hence, that Court observed that the plaintiffs are not entitled to get any order of temporary injunction against the co-sharer contesting defendant No. 6. The Court of appeal below also found that the balance of convenience and in-convenience was not in favour of the plaintiff’s petitioners and further found that the suit was only for declaration of title without any prayer for recovery or confirmation of possession or for permanent injunction. Upon the above findings, the learned Additional District Judge found the judgment and order of the trial Court to be legal and valid one and confirmed the same and dismissed the appeal on contest by his judgment and order dated 7.5.90. 

 3. Being aggrieved thereby the plaintiff-petitioners then moved the present application under Section 115(1) of the Code of Civil Procedure in this court and obtained the present Rule. At the time of the issuance of the Rule, on the prayer of the petitioners, this Court was pleased to grant an order of statusquo in respect of possession over the suit property till 21.10.90. But for want of prayer for extension in due course, the said order of statusquo expired on 21.10.90 and thereafter on the prayer of the petitioners by another application, the order of statusquo was again granted by a Bench of this Court till disposal of the Rule vide order dated 19.11.90. 

 5. Mr. Farid Ahmed, the learned Advocate for the petitioners, has contended that the Courts below committed an error of law resulting in an error in the decision occasioning a failure of justice by rejecting the application for temporary injunction of the petitioners without properly considering the prima-facie case of title and possession of the petitioners in the suit lands and also the question of balance of convenience and inconvenience of the parties together with the question of irreparable loss of the plaintiff-petitioners, if any. Hence the impugned orders of the Courts below cannot be sustained in law and facts and the same are liable to be set aside and the petitioners are entitled to get an order for temporary injunction against the opposite parties till disposal of the suit. 

 6. Mr. Abu Sayeed Ahmed the learned advocate appearing for the opposite parties. on the other hand, contends that the submissions of the learned Advocate for the petitioners have no legs to stand upon in as much as it is crystal clear from the judgments of the Courts below that both the Courts, on consideration of the materials on records, have rightly found that the contesting defendant No. 6, i.e. opposite party No. 1, obtained permanent settlement of 4 acres of land from the disputed plot, namely, C.S. Plot No. 2071 which originally belonged to the Bhawal Court of Wards. Estate, but was subsequently made khas by the Government after the promulgation of the State Acquisition and Tenancy Act, to the extent of 4.58 acres of land out of which the contesting defendant No 6 obtained the said permanent settlement of 4 acres of lands in his favour and went into actual possession of the same through legal process and has been continuing the possession by demarcating the boundaries with pillars and mutating his name and paying rents, and the balance of convenience and inconvenience has been rightly found to be in favour of the defendant No. 6 i.e. opposite party No. 1 and not in favour of the plaintiff-petitioners. Nextly, to show the prima-facie case for injunction, the plaintiff-petitioners could only produce a few papers namely dakhilas of payment of rents for portion of the suit-lands only and some papers to show the acquisition of some portion of the suit land by the Govt. for C & B. department and the Board of Cotton Development. But for the reasons best to the plaintiffs, those acquired lands have not been excluded from the suit lands and the above requiring bodies have not been made parties in the suit. 

 7. We have heard the learned Advocates and considered their submissions and perused the impugned orders and the connected papers. Now, when both the Courts have concurrently found possession of the defendant No. 6 i.e. opposite party No. 1 in his 4 acres of settled land of the disputed plot which has been demarcated by pillars, we find no justification to interfere with the impugned orders and allow any prayer for temporary injunction in favour of the plaintiff petitioner against the contesting defendant-opposite party No. 1 depriving him from enjoying his own property. Granting of temporary injunction is a matter of discretion with the Court but cannot be granted on mere asking, unless the Court is satisfied with the same in accordance with the settled principles in the facts and circumstances of the case. In the instant case, both the Courts on consideration of the materials on record, have come to concurrent findings, particularly on question of possession, and rejected the prayer for temporary injunction. 

 8. We, therefore, find no illegality in the impugned orders of the Courts below and the same have not occasioned any failure of justice. The plaintiff-petitioners are, therefore, not entitled to any order of temporary injunction in the facts and circumstances of the case, but in view of the fact that at the time of the issuance of the Rule, and thereafter, an order of statusquo was granted by this Court in respect of possession over the suit-property and the same has been still operating without any grievance from either of the parties, we deem it fit and proper in the exercise of our judicial discretion to keep the said order of statusquo still in force to avoid any clash or disturbance over the possession of the suit land till disposal of the suit. Before parting with this Rule, we would like to direct the trial Court to dispose of the suit as expeditiously as possible and the parties are directed to fully co-operate with the Court concerned in this regard. 

 10. Let a copy of this judgment and order be transmitted to the trial Court immediately.
